title: Regional Commitment Windows + Preemption Insurance: Pricing Pilot for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Alicia Chen
description:
Summary: Propose and validate a pilot pricing product that combines short-term regional commitment windows (e.g., 1/3/6 month locks per region) with an optional 'preemption insurance' add-on that compensates customers when we need to preempt or shift capacity for operational reasons. Goal is to capture enterprise customers who need predictability but are unwilling to sign long multi-region contracts.

Problem: Large customers want lower unit pricing and capacity guarantees but prefer the flexibility to avoid multi-year lockups. Existing reserved commits are either too rigid (annual) or too low-margin (hourly). We need a new SKU suite that: (1) enables shorter regional commitments with tiered discounts, (2) exposes a clear preemption policy and a compensatory credit mechanism (insurance), and (3) integrates with autoscaling/burst behavior and SLA tiers.

Hypothesis: Offering 1/3/6 month regional reservations with optional preemption insurance will increase closed-won rate for mid-market and enterprise accounts who require bounded commitments, and will increase ARR velocity while keeping capacity utilization >75% in targeted regions.

Success metrics (pilot):
- Win rate uplift for outbound enterprise deals involving dedicated capacity: +15% vs baseline within 3 months.
- Incremental ARR from regional-commit pilots: $250k+ within quarter for initial cohort.
- Average regional utilization of reserved pools >= 75% across pilot regions.
- Customer-reported satisfaction (NPS-like) for capacity predictability >= +10 points.

Proposed SKU constructs: 
1) Regional Commitment Window (RCW): 1-month / 3-month / 6-month term options, per-region. Pricing: graduated discounts vs on-demand (1-month: 10%, 3-month: 18%, 6-month: 28%). Commitments billed monthly but cancellable at window end.
2) Preemption Insurance Add-on (PIA): optional monthly add-on that pays customers in service credits for capacity preemption events that cause sustained performance degradation (exceeding defined threshold). Insurance tiers map to SLA tiers; higher-tier insurance reduces compensation latency.
3) Autoscale Burst Pool Integrations: policies that allow committed capacity to be borrowed by adjacent regions for brief windows; borrowing triggers higher per-minute overage rate and applies insurance differently.
4) SLA Tie-ins: map RCW + PIA combinations to three SLA tiers (Gold/Silver/Bronze) with explicit latency and availability targets and incident SLAs.

Operational considerations & trade-offs: 
- Revenue recognition and billing complexity: monthly billing for term commitments simplifies customer cash flow but increases internal billing churn. Finance has requested a draft accounting treatment.
- Capacity forecasting: shorter windows increase forecasting noise. We will hedge by reserving a small global buffer and using surge buckets.
- Legal & procurement: PIA needs explicit definition of preemption events and remedies; Legal will need SLA language and sample contract addendum.
- Risk to utilization: very aggressive discounts on short-term commitments could cannibalize longer commitments. We will gate pilot eligibility (no mix-and-match discounts across regions for pilot cohort).

Technical integration points: 
- Console: new UI for per-region commitment selection + insurance toggles, cost preview. (Design ticket DES-84211 placeholder.)
- Billing: billing platform must support monthly invoice line items with conditional credit issuance on preemption events.
- Runtime: autoscaler and routing must emit structured events for preemption/borrow events for metricization and automated credit calculations. (ENG work required: ENG-4312 existing stub.)

Rollout plan (3 phases):
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): Spec + legal term outline + finance modelling + internal pricing deck.
- Phase 1 (4 weeks): Pilot product build (console mockups, billing wiring, runtime event telemetry), sales enablement for 3 target customer pilots in NA West and EU West.
- Phase 2 (6 weeks): Run pilot, collect utilization/claims data, iterate pricing elasticity and insurance thresholds, finalize contract language and standard SKU.

Open questions for the cross-functional review: 
- What threshold defines a compensable preemption event? (SRE suggestion: >5 minutes sustained service degradation for >10% of tokens served in a 1-hour window.)
- How to price the PIA per GPU-hour to balance actuarial risk vs attractiveness? Finance wants tiered risk buckets.
- Can we automate insurance payments (credits) or require manual reconciliation?

Acceptance criteria:
- Finance approves unit economics model and ARR forecast for pilot.
- Legal approves sample contract language and PIA definition.
- Console mockups reviewed and queued in Cycle 2025-W12.
- Instrumentation for preemption events emitting consistent structured metrics and a demo credit calculation script completed.
